units.translation: corruptly for τοιοίδε τοί μοι [such things to me], which Schuetz restored.
in the corrupt letters μή [not] Hermann thought ἑτοίμη [ready] was hidden, with little probability.
such are the ready customs of the torch-bearers
everyone is ready to lament for the unfortunate.
yoked, he was ready as my trace-horse.

they brought libations more ready than laughter.
in the tenth (Wunder: tenth) year of this light I have come to you.

Thus from the copies for ἑτοίμως [readily].
as truly as insolence is the child of impiety.

well, rightly, as is fitting. It is joined with any verbs. Especially frequent are εὖ φρονεῖν [to be well-minded] (which means either to be wise or to be well-disposed, about which will be said under φρονέω), εὖ δρᾶν τινα [to do well to someone] to bestow a benefit on someone, to which is opposed εὖ πάσχειν [to be well-treated] to receive a benefit, εὖ πράσσειν [to fare well] to obtain something good. Wellauer collected examples of these and other verbs arranged according to the order of the plays, which we append, correcting those which Wellauer had used in corruptly written form.
εὖ [well], with the verb ἔχει [to have] supplied in thought.
which the scholiast explains as εὐτυχήσας [having been fortunate], εὖ πράξας [having fared well]: see under κυρέω.
where Hermann has τὰ δ᾽ εὖ ἔχοντ᾽ ἐμὸν κέρδος αὔξει τόδε [but this well-being increases my gain].
where αὖ [again] is more probable, which Paleius restored.
corrupt from ἢ [or], which Canter restored.
where εὖ [well] is suspect, which Hermann changed to αὖ [again].

it is most profitable to be wise but not to seem wise.
for the eye of one who is wise accuses you.

doing well, suffering well, being honored well.
